subject: Output exclusivity vs service rights — MSA/Order Form coordination
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@clientco.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clientco.com, procurement@clientco.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA redlines — output ownership and training prohibition (initial)

Rafael,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our proposed redlines to the MSA/order form. We need a firm commitment that: 1) ClientCo has exclusive title to any outputs derived from prompts we send, 2) Redwood will not use ClientCo inputs or outputs to train or improve models, and 3) any feedback or telemetry gathered by Redwood will be limited to anonymized service metrics and never used for product development without explicit opt-in.

These are deal blockers for our InfoSec and procurement teams. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these types of restrictions or, if not, what limited carveouts you can offer for the hosted offering.

Attachment: ClientCo_MSA_redlines_v1.docx

Best,
Maria Santos
Sr. Counsel — ClientCo


From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines — need legal + sales triage

Laura / Ben — forwarding ClientCo redlines. High level:
- They want exclusive ownership to outputs (broad language).
- Full training prohibition on any customer I/O.
- No usage of telemetry/feedback for product/model improvements unless explicitly opted-in.

Attachments: ClientCo_MSA_redlines_v1.docx

My take: exclusivity + full training ban on hosted model will be very difficult for us; it restricts obvious service fallbacks and telemetry-driven bug fixes. We should propose: (a) customer ownership of their specific outputs for commercial exploitation, (b) nonexclusive license for Redwood to use aggregated/anonymous telemetry to operate and improve the service, and (c) explicit opt-in for training on identifiable customer data.

Can legal propose compromise language for the order form that preserves our ability to operate (fallback models, telemetry, safety) while giving them commercial rights they require? Ben — can you confirm whether ClientCo is flexible on hosting mode (Dedicated or Private) — Dedicated would materially change our stance on training usage.

Thanks,
Rafael
Head of Sales, East — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines — need legal + sales triage

Rafael / Ben —

Thanks for the context. Quick legal read and proposed approach:

1) Output ownership: We should accept a customer-friendly clause that grants ClientCo broad rights to outputs for their internal and commercial use, but refuse exclusive title. Exclusive ownership prevents Redwood from providing features like shared improvements, anonymized examples for docs, and would create friction for SaaS analytics features. Proposed language: "Customer is granted ownership and perpetual, worldwide rights to Customer Outputs for Customer's business purposes; Redwood retains the right to use de-identified, aggregated Outputs for service improvement and compliance purposes."

2) Training prohibition: We can accept a strict opt-out model for training on identifiable inputs/outputs if the customer opts for Dedicated or Private deployment. For hosted (shared) customers, limit to: "Redwood will not use Customer Inputs or Customer Outputs to train foundation models without Customer's prior written consent; Redwood may use aggregated telemetry and operational data to maintain, secure, and improve the Service." This preserves operational safety fixes.

3) Feedback/telemetry: We should be explicit that telemetry needed to meet SLAs and for security (e.g., anomaly detection, abuse signals) is excluded from the training prohibition. Also propose a short Exhibit A summarizing what telemetry categories are collected.

I'll draft redline suggestions (short, bulleted) and attach Redwood_response_draft_v1.docx for review. If Ben confirms Dedicated as an option, I'll prepare alternative clauses that grant stricter promises under a Dedicated/Private deployment schedule.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_response_draft_v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: maria.santos@clientco.com
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — output ownership and training prohibition (proposal)

Maria —

Thanks for sending the redlines. We appreciate the clarity on ClientCo's priorities. We want to resolve this quickly. High-level proposal attached (Redwood_response_draft_v1.docx) — summary below:

- Customer Outputs: ClientCo receives full ownership and a perpetual, worldwide license to use, modify, and redistribute Outputs. We do not accept an exclusive assignment.
- Training & Model Use: Redwood will not use Customer Inputs/Outputs to train foundation models or include them in public training sets without explicit, documented consent. For hosted customers, Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for service improvements; for Dedicated/Private deployments, we can offer a contractual opt-in/opt-out schedule that meets your governance needs.
- Telemetry & Feedback: We will exclude telemetry that contains PII or raw customer content from any model training. Operational telemetry (latency, error rates, anonymized usage counts) may be used to maintain the service; we will document categories in Exhibit A.

If you have an appetite for Dedicated capacity, we can draft a stronger training prohibition in the order form tied to Dedicated subscription commitments. Can we schedule a short call Thurs to review redlines?

Cheers,
Ben
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_response_draft_v1.docx

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@clientco.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clientco.com, procurement@clientco.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — output ownership and training prohibition (follow-up)

Ben / Rafael / Laura —

Thank you for the quick turnaround and the draft. A few clarifications from our side after legal reviewed:
- ClientCo cannot accept any language that allows Redwood to retain rights to "de-identified" outputs for product training — our legal and privacy teams are concerned "de-identification" is not reversible in all cases and could be reanalyzed. If Redwood wants a training pathway, it must be an explicit opt-in with clear scope and narrow data handling requirements.
- Telemetry that could contain business-sensitive signals (usage patterns tied to API keys) must be contractually excluded from product improvement unless anonymized at a strict hashing level.

We appreciate the Dedicated/Private option and would like a redline that ties the stricter prohibitions to an on-prem or VPC-hosted deployment. Please include concrete language for Exhibit A showing categories we agree can be collected under each deployment mode.

Also, procurement requests a timeline for legal review and final order form — we are targeting a signature by Nov 30.

Regards,
Maria
Sr. Counsel — ClientCo

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: maria.santos@clientco.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — output ownership and training prohibition (next steps)

Maria — thanks. We can meet the Nov 30 timetable with a few action items and an optional Dedicated path. Proposed next steps:

1) Laura to issue a redline set that: a) grants ClientCo ownership and a perpetual license for Outputs, b) explicitly bars Redwood from using Customer Inputs/Outputs to train foundation models without written consent (and ties stricter guarantees to Dedicated/Private deployments), and c) narrows "de-identified" language and adds handling requirements.

2) Ben to confirm procurement terms for Dedicated pricing and to provide a one-page SOW option.

3) Rafael to schedule a 30-min legal sync with ClientCo (available Fri 13th or Mon 16th).

Laura — if you can attach the redline and a short Exhibit A (service telemetry categories by deployment mode), we'll circulate for ClientCo's legal and procurement.

I'll set up a DocuSign draft once we have redlines with the Dedicated addendum.

Best,
Rafael
Head of Sales, East — Redwood Inference

Attachment: ExhibitA-Service-Rights-Summary.pdf
